instructions: Grate the carrots on the large holes of a box grater. That should be about 3 cups.
Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the carrots and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until the carrots are soft and no longer crunchy.
Spread the carrots out on a plate and let them cool completely, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, crush the garlic to a paste and stir it into the yogurt in a serving bowl.
Fold the cooled carrots into the yogurt. If the carrots are still warm, the yogurt turns thin.
Taste it. If it's flat, add the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Drizzle the last 1 tbsp olive oil over the top and serve with cut vegetables or bread. It keeps in a covered container in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze it.
method_notes: Jamil Ghar (5 out of 5 from 3 votes, so below the 20 ratings needed) and Cooking Gorgeous agree on grated carrots sautéed in olive oil until soft, cooled, then folded into thick yogurt with raw garlic. They differ on the carrot-to-yogurt ratio, with Jamil Ghar using far more carrot. This lands between them. Both finish with crushed walnuts; they are left out to keep it nut-free.
